author: Povilas Adomas Brukas
description: Build and host websites from Claude, ChatGPT or Claude Code. Your AI writes the site, Ginta publishes it live on yourname.ginta.page. Includes working forms, menus, bookings, blogs, an owner /admin, encrypted API keys and build uploads. OAuth sign-in, free tier.
name: Ginta

tools.name: get_guide
tools.title: Read the Ginta building guide
tools.description: Returns Ginta's building guide: how Ginta sites work, the design brief, functional blocks and SEO. Use before building or editing a site. topic "developers" = file uploads, builds, redirects and API connections only; "modules" = the live parts.

topic.description: The topic returned (all, design, blocks, editing, seo, modules, developers).

chars.description: Length of the guide text, which is in the text content.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.title: The user's websites, plan and limits
tools.description: Use when you need a site_id, or the user asks about their websites, plan, limits, credits or page views. Lists every site with its URL and form message count, plus what the plan allows.

annotations.title: The user's websites, plan and limits

credits.description: Credits for Ginta's own in-app AI.

page_views_this_month.description: Page views of all websites this month.

account.description: Plan, limits and usage of the signed-in account.

badge.description: The "Made with Ginta" badge: whether it shows and why.

tools.name: check_name
tools.title: Check if a site name is free
tools.description: Use before create_site when the user wants a specific address (https://<name>.ginta.page); suggests alternatives if taken. "Bella Roma" becomes "bella-roma".

name.description: Wanted name, e.g. the business name.

annotations.title: Check if a site name is free

name.description: The name as a site id (lowercase, hyphens).

reason.description: Why not, if taken or not allowed.

tools.name: get_site
tools.title: Read a site: files and versions
tools.description: Use before editing an existing site, or when the owner wants their code: returns its files (text contents; images and fonts as a list with their addresses), and with history: true its saved versions for restore_version. Pass paths to read only some files. (In Ginta, owners on Hosting Plus, Hosting Studio, Pro, Agency can also download everything as a .zip from the website's ⋯ menu.)

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

paths.description: Only these files (default: all text files, if the site isn't too large).

history.description: Also list the last 20 saved versions.

annotations.title: Read a site: files and versions

notify_email.description: Form messages go here (null = the account email).

files.description: Text files returned (their contents are in the text content).

assets.description: Images, fonts and other binary files.

complete.description: false = the site is too large; ask for specific paths.

tools.name: get_stats
tools.title: Visitors, speed and SEO of a site
tools.description: Use when the user asks how many visitors their site gets or how fast and well-built it is: views per day (30 days), top pages, referring websites, and the phone scores (performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO) with the issues to fix.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

annotations.title: Visitors, speed and SEO of a site

visitors.description: Page views in the last 30 days.

speed.description: The latest phone speed check (PageSpeed scores and issues).

tools.name: create_site
tools.title: Publish a new website
tools.description: Publishes a NEW website in the user's account and returns its URL; building one takes about 1–3 minutes. Takes the files you designed (index.html required; see get_guide), or no files to get an upload link for a build. Pages should hold only real details the user gave (phone numbers, addresses, prices, reviews). note is required: what you built and why.

name.description: Site name for the URL (optional; random if omitted).

files.description: All files of the site (index.html required). Omit to get an upload link for a .zip build instead.

content.description: Text content (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, SVG…).

content_base64.description: Binary files (images, fonts, PDF…): the bytes, base64-encoded.

notify_email.description: Only if form messages should go to another address than the owner's Ginta account email (the default, every plan).

layout.description: The layout idea from get_guide section 4 closest to your page, or "custom".

aesthetic.description: The named art direction from your brief, e.g. "1970s municipal pool signage".

fonts.description: Font families used, e.g. "Anton / Work Sans".

note.description: REQUIRED. 1–2 plain sentences: what you changed and why, e.g. "Rebuilt the menu page, added lunch prices, moved contact to the footer." The owner sees it in Ginta's editor; Ginta's own AI reads it.

notify_email.description: Another address for form messages, if set.

notices.description: Sentences to tell the owner word for word.

problems.description: Things that don't work: fix them.

empty.description: Parts the owner asked for that are still empty.

check.description: Ginta's visitor check of the site: forms, parts, links.

upload.description: When no files were sent: the upload link for a .zip build.

mode.description: replace = the zip becomes the whole site; merge = adds/replaces files.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working (ISO time).

command.description: Shell command that zips dist/ and uploads it.

tools.name: update_site
tools.title: Change a website
tools.description: Changes an existing site's pages: small find/replace edits (preferred), whole files, deleted files, or the form email; a change takes about 1–3 minutes. All changes apply together as one new version (undo with restore_version). note is required: what you changed and why.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

find.description: Exact text currently in the file (must occur once; include a bit of surrounding text to make it unique).

replace.description: Text to put instead (empty string deletes).

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

files.description: Whole files to add or replace (only the changed ones).

content.description: Text content (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, SVG…).

content_base64.description: Binary files (images, fonts, PDF…): the bytes, base64-encoded.

delete.description: Paths of files to delete (not index.html).

notify_email.description: Another address for form messages ("" = back to the account email).

note.description: REQUIRED. 1–2 plain sentences: what you changed and why, e.g. "Rebuilt the menu page, added lunch prices, moved contact to the footer." The owner sees it in Ginta's editor; Ginta's own AI reads it.

warnings.description: Things to look at (the change was saved).

notices.description: Sentences to tell the owner word for word.

problems.description: Things that don't work: fix them.

empty.description: Parts the owner asked for that are still empty.

check.description: Ginta's visitor check of the site: forms, parts, links.

notify_email.description: Where form messages go (null = the account email).

tools.name: upload_files
tools.title: Upload many files (images, fonts, a build)
tools.description: Use for images, fonts and other binary files, many files at once, or a whole build (Vite/Astro/Next export): send files (text, base64 or a link), or no files to get an upload link you POST a .zip of the build to with curl. note is required: what you changed and why.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

files.description: Files to add or replace. Omit to get an upload link for a .zip.

content.description: Text content (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, SVG…).

content_base64.description: Binary files (images, fonts, PDF…): the bytes, base64-encoded.

url.description: Instead of content: a public link Ginta downloads (an image, a font, a file on GitHub…).

replace_all.description: The upload becomes the whole site: files not in it are deleted (for a fresh build). Default false (merge).

note.description: REQUIRED. 1–2 plain sentences: what you changed and why, e.g. "Rebuilt the menu page, added lunch prices, moved contact to the footer." The owner sees it in Ginta's editor; Ginta's own AI reads it.

annotations.title: Upload many files (images, fonts, a build)

version.description: The new live version (after an upload).

notices.description: Sentences to tell the owner word for word.

problems.description: Things that don't work: fix them.

empty.description: Parts the owner asked for that are still empty.

check.description: Ginta's visitor check of the site: forms, parts, links.

upload_url.description: Without files: where to POST the .zip.

command.description: Without files: the command that uploads the build.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.title: Undo: restore a previous version
tools.description: Use to undo changes: restores a saved version (numbers from get_site with history: true) as a new version, so it can itself be undone.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

tools.name: preview_site
tools.title: Look at a site (screenshots)
tools.description: Use after create_site or a bigger change to see the page like a visitor: desktop (1280 px, top to bottom) and phone (390 px) screenshots of one page. Limited per day by plan; if none are left, review the HTML instead.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

page.description: Page to look at, e.g. "menu" (default: the home page).

url.description: The page that was looked at.

available.description: false = no screenshots right now; review the HTML instead.

tools.name: attach_image
tools.title: Put the owner's photo or logo online
tools.description: Use for the owner's own photos and logo in business sites and module content (menu, shop, gallery, blog): copies one image (a public link or base64) into their account and returns a /_g/u/… path to use in HTML or module data.

url.description: Public http(s) link to the image file.

data_base64.description: The image file itself, base64-encoded (instead of url).

annotations.title: Put the owner's photo or logo online

path.description: Path to use in HTML or module data, e.g. /_g/u/abc.webp.

tools.name: get_messages
tools.title: Read the site's form messages
tools.description: Use when the user asks for their form messages, enquiries or contact requests: messages visitors sent through the site's forms, newest first. They hold visitors' personal data, for the site's owner.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

tools.name: manage_module
tools.title: Live parts: menu, bookings, shop, blog…
tools.description: Use to set up or change the live parts the owner manages (prices, bookings, products, posts, photos, events, quote requests, notices), without rewriting pages. Modules and actions: collections (list, define, get, save_item, delete_item, import, delete_collection); announcements (list, post, setup, delete); menu (get, setup, save_item, delete_item); gallery (get, add_photos, delete_photo); blog (list, save, delete); bookings (get, setup, list, cancel, add_days_off); catalog (get, setup, save_product, delete_product, list_orders); quote (setup, list, update); events (list, save, cancel, list_signups). action "help" shows a module's fields; omit module to see what the plan includes.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

module.description: Which module (omit to list them all for this site).

action.description: What to do, e.g. "setup", "get", "list", "save_item" (see above); "help" for the fields.

data.description: The action's fields (see help), e.g. for menu setup {"sections": [...]}.

annotations.title: Live parts: menu, bookings, shop, blog…

outputSchema.description: Depends on the call: without module, { site_id, modules: [{ id, name, included, active, snippet }] }; with help, { module, actions: [{ action, read_only }] }; otherwise the action's own result (e.g. the saved item or a list).

tools.name: manage_admins
tools.title: Who can manage a website at its /admin
tools.description: Use when the owner says who should keep the website up to date (e.g. "add maria@salon.lt as admin"), for example after building a site with parts the owner fills in. Admin users sign in at <website>/admin with their email and a password (no Ginta account) and change its lists, menu, bookings… and read its messages; never the design or code. add: with a password the owner chose, or without one (they get an email to choose their own). set_password: for an admin user, or the owner's own email to give the owner a password for this site. send_setup_link: a new "choose your password" email.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

action.description: What to do: list the admin users, add or remove one, set_password, or send_setup_link (a new choose-your-password email).

email.description: Their email address (every action but list).

password.description: Only if the owner gave one (8+ characters; add, set_password). Never invent one; never repeat it in the chat.

annotations.title: Who can manage a website at its /admin

limit.description: list: admin users allowed on this plan.

has_admin.description: Whether the site has anything to manage at /admin.

outputSchema.description: Depends on the action (list, add, remove, set_password, send_setup_link).

tools.name: manage_secrets
tools.title: API keys of a site (write-only)
tools.description: Use when the site needs an API key (weather, CRM, maps…): set stores it encrypted, list shows names only, delete removes one. Values can never be read back, by you or anyone; use them through manage_connections.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

action.description: What to do: list the names, set (save or replace) one, or delete one.

name.description: Secret name in capitals, e.g. "WEATHER_API_KEY" (set, delete).

value.description: The key itself (set only). Ask the user to paste it; never invent one.

tools.name: manage_connections
tools.title: Let a site call an API with a secret
tools.description: Use when the site's JavaScript must call an outside API: save a connection (name, https base URL, which secret, how it's sent), and the page calls fetch("/_ginta/api/<name>/<path>"); Ginta adds the key and forwards to that base URL only. list shows connections and this month's calls.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

action.description: What to do: list the connections, save (add or change) one, or delete one.

base_url.description: The API's https base URL, e.g. "https://api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5".

secret.description: Name of the secret to attach (from manage_secrets). Omit for public APIs.

auth.description: How the key is sent: "bearer" (Authorization: Bearer, default), "header" (auth_name = the header, e.g. X-API-Key) or "query" (auth_name = the parameter, e.g. appid).

auth_name.description: Header or query parameter name for auth header/query.

annotations.title: Let a site call an API with a secret

tools.name: connect_domain
tools.title: Connect the user's own domain (or check it)
tools.description: Use when the user wants their own domain (e.g. "bakery.com") on a site, or asks whether it works yet: with domain it connects it (bakery.com shows the site, www.bakery.com redirects to it) and returns the exact DNS steps for their provider to relay (a record for the domain, a CNAME for www, and a TXT record proving the domain is theirs: the site is not served until it is seen); without domain it checks the status (pending, verifying, active) and whether https://bakery.com opens.

site_id.description: The site id: the first part of the site URL, e.g. "bella-roma" for https://bella-roma.ginta.page (see list_sites).

domain.description: The domain, e.g. "bakery.com" or "shop.bakery.com". Omit to check the current one.

with_www.description: Only if the user wants www.bakery.com as the main address (bakery.com then redirects to it). Default: bakery.com is the main address.

annotations.title: Connect the user's own domain (or check it)

domain.description: The domain: state (pending, verifying, active, error), records and the steps for its DNS provider; null = none.
